VS

full_judgment:
Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, J : By the instant Rule, the petitioner has challenged the legality and propriety of the Memo No. 114/BCe dated 25-6-2001, issued by respondent No. 1, initiating a Certificate Case, as well as the proceeding of the Certificate Case No. 70 of 2002, pending before respondent No. 2, as evidenced by Annexures A and A(1) respectively. 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, all further proceedings of Certificate Case No. 70 of 2002, pending before respondent No. 2 (General Certificate Officer, General Certificate Adalat, Collectorate Building, Dhaka), was stayed for a period of 4 (four) months. Subsequently, the aforesaid period of stay was extended from time to time by orders of different dates. 

 5. The petitioner came to learn from a notice published on 4-9-2004 in the daily 'Manab Jamin' by the Dhaka City Corporation that he was alleged to have taken lease (dl) of Gabtali Hat for the financial year 1997-1998 from respondent No. 1. It was also stated in the said notice that the petitioner had failed to pay 15% VAT and on account of such failure, respondent No. 1 had initiated a case against him for recovery of VAT amounting to Taka 59,00,000 (Taka Fifty Nine Lacs). By the aforesaid notice, information relating to the whereabouts of the petitioner was also sought from the public, which had been published along with a picture of the petitioner. However, although the address of the petitioner in the said notice was shown to be 7 RK Mission Road, Dhaka, the petitioner never resided in the said address, his correct address being 35/2, Shantinagar Peer Shaheber Goli, Dhaka. 

 6. Apprehending that some fraudulent activities might have been committed using his name, the petitioner issued a Legal Notice on 8-9-2004 upon respondent No. 1 stating that he never took lease of the Gabtali Hat. However, as respondent No. 1 did not respond to the said Legal Notice, the petitioner appeared in the Certificate Case and filed an application dated 12-9-2004 to discharge him from the said case stating that he had no knowledge or nexus with the lease of Gabtali Hat for the year 1997-1998. By order dated 20-9-2004, respondent No. 2 fixed 2-10-2004 as the next date for hearing of the petitioner's application. However, the said application has not yet been disposed of by the concerned respondent. 

 8. In the meantime, the petitioner inquired about the matter with the concerned respondents and came to learn that some interested quarters had used his name and photograph disclosing a fictitious address and submitted a tender with the Dhaka City Corporation for taking lease of Gabtali Hat. As the bid submitted by the said person was declared to be the highest, they were given lease of the Hat and they were also directed to pay 15% VAT and 3% advance Income tax. A lease was executed by Dhaka City Corporation and the possession of the hat was handed over on 2-9-1997 in presence of the local Member of Parliament. It is in the backdrop of the facts and circumstances noted above that the petitioner moved this Court challenging the aforesaid notice of the Certificate Case along with the proceeding of the said case. 

 9. Ms. Farzana Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, having placed the instant application together with the documents annexed thereto, submits that the demand made by the City Corporation is hit by the principle of coram non judice as the City Corporation has no authority under the law to demand payment of VAT from any individual. Elaborating her submission, the learned Advocate contends that even if it is accepted, but not conceded, that the petitioner is liable to pay a certain amount of VAT, as claimed by the respondent, yet, for realization of unpaid VAT, the City Corporation has no authority to initiate a Certificate Case, as has been done in the instant case. 

 10. Referring to Chapter II of the Dhaka City Corporation Ordinance, 1983 (hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance), which deals with "Corporation Taxes", in particular to sections 67, 68 and 72 thereof, the learned Advocate submits that the Corporation is empowered to levy any tax, rates, cesses, tolls and fees mentioned in the Second Schedule of the Ordinance. Turning now to the Second Schedule of the Ordinance, the learned Advocate submits that although the Second Schedule contains as many as 26 heads or categories under which the City Corporation may levy tax, it does not include VAT. In other words, according to the learned Advocate, the Dhaka City Corporation has not been empowered by or under the Second Schedule to demand or realize any VAT from an individual and that also by filing a Certificate Case. 

 11. Referring to section 72 of the Ordinance, Ms. Khan submits that although the Corporation is empowered to recover arrears of taxes, rates, cesses tolls and fees as a public demand by filing a Certificate Case, it does not authorize the Corporation to realize unpaid or arrear VAT. Referring to the provisions of the Value Added Tax Act, 1991 (briefly the Act) in particular to sections 55 and 56 thereof, the learned Advocate submits that it is the concerned VAT officials of the National Board of Revenue, who have been specifically empowered by this Act to make a demand for realization of any unpaid or less paid VAT. However, such a demand has to be preceded by issuance of a show cause notice. 

 12. The learned Advocate submits that a demand for unpaid VAT has to be made within a period of 3 (three) years from the date on which it became due. However, in the instant case, the demand was made beyond the period of three years and therefore, the said demand is barred by limitation. She forcefully submits that since the statutory provision namely, the VAT Act, is very much in existence to deal with the issue of non-payment or less payment of VAT, the initiation of a Certificate Case for realization of unpaid VAT by the City Corporation is palpably without lawful authority and therefore, the instant Rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 13. On the other hand, the Rule is being opposed by respondent No. 1 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition. Mr Saha, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the contesting respondent No. 1 submits that the Dhaka City Corporation (briefly, the DCC) granted lease of the Gabtali Hat for 1997-1998 to the petitioner. However, on account of non-payment of 15% VAT of the lease money, the Certificate Case was initiated by the Corporation. He submits forcefully that as the lease was granted by the City Corporation and the lease money in respect of such lease was received by the City Corporation, the non-payment of VAT in relation to the said lease money can be realized by DCC by filing a Certificate Case. 

 16. It is to be noted at the outset that although the petitioner has denied to have ever applied for the lease, the respondents have asserted that it is the petitioner who took lease of the hat. These assertions and denial give raise to a disputed question of fact, which, admittedly, cannot be decided in the writ jurisdiction by this Court and we certainly do not intend to do so. What we are called upon to decide in this Rule is the legal authority of DCC to file a Certificate Case for realization of unpaid  VAT. 

 19. Section 72 of the Ordinance provides that for purpose of collection and recovery of the taxes, the Corporation may recover the same as a public demand. In other words, the Corporation is empowered to file a Certificate Case for the realization of all "arrears of taxes, rates, cesses, tolls and fees and other money claimable by the Corporation under the Ordinance." 

 22. During the course of his submission, Mr Saha referred to section 24 of the Value Added Tax Rules, 1991 and tried to impress upon the Court that under section 24 of the Rules, the City Corporation is bound to provide assistance to the VAT official (মূল্য সংযোজন কর কর্মকর্তা)in discharging his duties. Relying on the aforesaid provision, the learned Advocate contends that it is apparent that the City Corporation can also initiate a Certificate Case for realization of unpaid VAT, as has been done in the instant case. In our view, the submission is misconceived since that rendering assistance is one thing, initiating a certificate case demanding unpaid VAT is completely another thing. 

 23. During the course of her submission, Ms. Khan has relied on section 55(1) of the VAT Act, 1991, (which was in force at the relevant time) to substantiate her contention that the demand as well as the initiation of the Certificate Case demanding payment of arrear VAT was also barred by law as the said demand was made beyond the statutory period. The learned Advocate further submits that as the demand in question related to the fiscal year 1997-1998, the legal provisions, which were prevailing at the relevant time, shall apply to the instant case. The learned Advocate acknowledges that relevant section has been amended subsequently where the period of limitation has been stated to be 5 years, but the same will not apply to the present case. 

 24. On the issue of limitation, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 1 submits that the concerned officer of the Dhaka City Corporation sent a Memo to the General Certificate Officer, Collectorate Building, Dhaka on 25-6-2001 to accept the Certificate Case under the PDR Act for realization of unpaid VAT from the petitioner in respect of the fiscal year 1997-1998 amounting to Taka 59,00,000 He submits that the said application having been filed on 25-6-2001, it was within the statutory period of three years. 

 25. On the other hand, Ms. Farzana Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has referred to Annexure A(1) and submits that the Certificate Case No. 70 of 2002 was initiated on 4-5-2002, as is evident from the order of the same date and therefore, the said case was initiated beyond the statutory period of 3 (three) years. 

 26. In course of her submission, the learned Advocate for the petitioner has referred to the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Moulavi Bazar vs Pirpur Fisherman's Co-operative Society Limited, reported in VI ADC (2009) 451 wherein the Apex Court decided that a writ petition is maintainable challenging the proceeding of a Certificate Case filed under the PDR Act, when the same is filed without lawful authority. Ms. Khan also referred to the case of Md Zakir Ahmed vs National Board of Revenue, reported in 20 BLC 37, wherein a Division Bench of this Court held that prior to making a demand for unpaid VAT, the authorities are required to issue a show cause notice under section 55 (3).

 28. Ms. Khan has also referred to the case of Mahmudul Islam vs ACC, reported in 61 DLR 361. wherein the Anti-Corruption Commission issued a Memo claiming unpaid VAT from the petitioner. While making the Rule absolute, the Court held as under: 

 29. In the case of AA Engineering Limited vs University of Khulna, reported in 66 DLR (AD) 19, the Court held as under: 

 30. On the other hand, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent has referred to an unreported decision of this Court passed in Writ Petition No. 995 of 2006. (Shuvash Chandra Das vs National Board of Revenue). Mr Saha submits that in the aforesaid decision, the authority of the General Certificate Officer to file a case for realization of unpaid VAT was challenged. However, a Division Bench of this Court by judgment dated 17-2-2016 discharged the Rule holding as under: 

 31. In our view, the decision referred to above is distinguishable from the present case before us as because in the aforesaid case, the General Certificate Officer initiated the Certificate Case at the behest of the VAT Officer. 

 32. The contesting respondent has next referred to another unreported decision of this Court in Writ Petition No. 4940 of 2004 (Mojibur Rahman Chowdhury vs National Board of Revenue and others), wherein a Division Bench of this Court, by judgment dated 12-1-2016, discharged the Rule holding that a Certificate Case can be maintained by the General Certificate Office, which was initiated at the instance of Customs official under section 202 of the Customs Act, 1999. Once again the said case is distinguishable from the present case before us. 

 33. It is to be noted that in both the unreported judgments relied upon by respondent No. 1, the filing of the certificate case by the General Certificate Officer was declared to be with lawful authority and consequently the Rule was discharged as the initiation of the respective cases was made by the proper authority, as designated under the relevant law. However, in the instant case, admittedly, the certificate case was initiated by the Dhaka City Corporation claiming unpaid VAT. Although Second Schedule of the Ordinance enumerates as many as 26 heads or categories under which the City Corporation can make a demand, it does not include VAT. Moreover, the filing of the Certificate case was not made at the request or behest of the concerned VAT Authority. Therefore, in our view, the issuance of the demand and the filing of the certificate case by the City Corporation cannot be said to have been made in accordance with law. 

 36. The Memo No. 114 /BCe dated 25-6-2001, issued by respondent No. 1, initiating Certificate Case No. 70 of 2002 as well as the continuation of the proceeding of the Certificate case, pending before respondent No. 2, as evidenced by Annexures A and A(1) respectively is hereby declared to be without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect.
